newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called to open little changed.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open little changed Tuesday following a steady ACCESS session, market sources said.
August over-the-counter trade wavered between $2.08 and $2.09 after settling Monday at $2.085 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, August crawled one cent to a high of $2.095 before last trading up only 0.1 cent at $2.086.
Chart traders pegged August support at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week was seen around $2.22, with further resistance at $2.29 and $2.36.
"If it (August) does pop, it will probably get sold off pretty quickly," one trader said.

In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices skidded almost ten cents to the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes were off more than five cents to $2.05-2.06, while New York city gate gas fell 15 cents to about $2.40.

Cooler-than-normal weather throughout most of the Northeast and Midwest this week was expected to keep pressure on cash prices. More moderate temperatures are forecast for this weekend, rising to above-normal levels in the East early next week, Weather Services Corp reported.
Separately, early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report were about 69 bcf.
